Adding a few technical notes for the rehearsal so we don't get bogged down in minutiae live:

- Operator roles: Redwood recommends separating the HSM operator (physical/console) from the KMS operator (software key import/rotation). The rehearsal should show both flows.
- Rotation model: demo importing a wrapped key (BYOK) into the HSM, then a scheduled rotation using the KMS with dual-sign off. We'll also show emergency key compromise remediation (revoke + fallback to model-variant routing).
- Network: we prefer restricting HSM control plane to a private management subnet and expose only a single well-documented port range to your bastion; avoid public egress on the HSM box.
- Audit artifacts: we will generate signed rotation manifests (GPG-signed blob), operator access events (syslog + SSO session id), and per-rotation KDF parameters. Confirm auditors accept signed manifests.

I'll present the sealed-key operator checklist segment (short) and coordinate the demo steps with Tessa.

Mina Haddad
Product Security, Redwood Inference
From: SafeHSM Support <support@safehsm.com>

Hi Alice / Sergio,

Thanks for the heads-up. Quick answers to your two outstanding items:

- HSM model: Globex indicated SafeHSM-v3 in your intake; SafeHSM-v3 supports both on-device split-key unlock (N-of-M) and an external consensus unlock via our KeyBroker. If you want to avoid additional network hops, use the on-device split-key feature.
- Operator tooling: We provide an operator agent (daemon) that runs in a hardened management subnet. It communicates to the HSM over the vendor management port (TCP 9901) and supports mTLS to our KeyBroker if you go external-escrow.

Attached is an estimate/quote and short admin guide. Note: on-device split-key is slightly faster to operate but you'll need at least three custodians trained for N-of-M.

Attachment stubs:
- safehsm-estimate-quote.pdf (application/pdf)
- safehsm-admin-quickstart.pdf (application/pdf)

Regards,
SafeHSM Support Team
